facts.text: Williams Acres sits in the western part of McKinley County, tucked into the Puerco River valley, a westward tributary of the Little Colorado.
Historic Route 66, now New Mexico State Road 118, cuts through the northern edge of Williams Acres, echoing the town’s early highway heritage.
The Gallup Subdivision of the BNSF Railway borders Williams Acres to the north, while Interstate 40 lies just south of the community.
Williams Acres is part of the Gallup‑McKinley County Public Schools district, with students attending Tobe Turpen Elementary, Chief Manualito Middle, and Gallup High.
The community’s geographic coordinates place it at latitude 35.4969 and longitude ‑108.87, right in the heart of McKinley County.
Williams Acres is a census‑designated place, meaning it has no formal government but is recognized for statistical purposes.
